capabilities.name: Audit Log
capabilities.description: Admin audit log: who changed what, and when. Server actions call writeAuditLog (src/modules/audit); admins read it at /admin/audit-log, linked from Settings. Mapp Team access changes are recorded out of the box. Also covers the older per-account customer activity tracking (page visits, custom events). Always included in the template.

capabilities.name: Client Catalog
capabilities.description: Discover companies and workspaces from Mapp's Company Management Service (GUM). Uses V2 API. Authenticates via the shared internal-API credential (Keycloak realm s2s, INTERNAL_API_*), with Basic Auth as a QA-only fallback. Companies map to Accounts, workspaces serve multiple products via services array (INTELLIGENCE, ST, ENGAGE, FASHION).

envVarSources._note: Do not invent these values and do not ask the app owner for them. THE SHARED SSM NAMESPACE IS PER-ENVIRONMENT: /mapp-labs for production, /mapp-labs-stg for staging (/mapp-labs-<shortEnv> otherwise). A staging app that reads /mapp-labs/* silently talks to PRODUCTION — it works, so the mistake is invisible. The s2s client id is 'mapp-labs' in both, but the SECRET differs per realm: a production secret returns unauthorized_client against INT. Read from account 936190502406, eu-central-1, profile labs-power. See docs/template/INTERNAL-API.md. CLIENT_CATALOG_BASE_URL is likewise PER-ENVIRONMENT and is NOT a constant — it must come from the same environment as the credential above or the token is rejected.

Add Workspace model: clientCatalogWorkspaceId (Int @unique, route key), clientCatalogCompanyId (Int, scope + relation key), name, tenantId, systemId, dashboardSystemId, services (Json), metadata (Json)

envVarSources._note: The INTERNAL_API_* credential is shared with client_catalog and every other internal Mapp service — read it from shared SSM, do not create a UPC-specific OAuth trio. THE SHARED SSM NAMESPACE IS PER-ENVIRONMENT: /mapp-labs for production, /mapp-labs-stg for staging (/mapp-labs-<shortEnv> otherwise). A staging app that reads /mapp-labs/* silently talks to PRODUCTION — it works, so the mistake is invisible. The s2s client id is 'mapp-labs' in both, but the SECRET differs per realm: a production secret returns unauthorized_client against INT. Read from account 936190502406, eu-central-1, profile labs-power. See docs/template/INTERNAL-API.md. UPC_API_BASE_URL has no shared SSM parameter yet; ask the labs-platform team, and make sure the URL you are given is for the same environment as the credential.

capabilities.name: Company Login (Keycloak / Mapp Cloud)
capabilities.description: Keycloak-brokered auth with a company-context customer path. One Keycloak provider, two IdP hints: 'Mapp Entra ID' -> internal Mapp admins, 'Company Login' (mapp-cloud-company) -> Mapp Cloud customers whose session is enriched on login with companyId / tenantId / workspaces[].services and persisted to a CompanyUser row for durable usage attribution. Built into the template auth module; the admin Company Users views show for apps that configure KEYCLOAK_COMPANY_IDP_HINT. App-specific behavior is injected via two seams: resolveAccountIdForCompany(companyId) (company->local Account mapping, template default returns null) and the CustomerEligibilityPolicy (entitlement gate, template default allow-all).

capabilities.name: Dev Login Bypass
capabilities.description: Local-only mock IdP so developers can sign in WITHOUT AWS or Keycloak. The /auth/dev page lets you pick admin or company-customer and runs the REAL signIn hydration + eligibility code (only the identity is mocked). DOUBLE-GATED: honored only when DEV_AUTH_ENABLED=true AND NODE_ENV!=production; the route 404s in production. Useful for every app (internal-only too).

capabilities.name: Keycloak API Token Auth
capabilities.description: Accept Keycloak-issued OAuth2 bearer tokens on your API routes (machine-to-machine / SSO-token callers), validated against the realm JWKS. Provides withKeycloak (bearer-only) and withHybridAuth (NextAuth admin session OR bearer) route wrappers, plus a /api/health-keycloak probe. Originated from CONNECT-1446; ships in the template auth module. Requires KEYCLOAK_ISSUER.

capabilities.name: Customer Preview (View as customer)
capabilities.description: An admin-level Mapp user previews a company's customer-facing /account pages exactly as that company's Company-Login customers see them: read-only, 30 minutes, bound to the admin, audited (customer_preview_start / customer_preview_end on entity type company). Optionally narrowed to one workspace. A signed cookie makes requireCustomer return a synthesized customer session, so eligibility, company context and every customer page run unchanged. Launch points on /admin/company-users and the client_catalog Companies scaffold. Off by default (CUSTOMER_PREVIEW_ENABLED). Use when admins/support need to see what a customer sees, check onboarding/eligibility, or demo a customer's view.

envVarSources._note: No secrets and nothing in SSM: CUSTOMER_PREVIEW_ENABLED=true turns it on; CUSTOMER_PREVIEW_SERVICES is the comma-separated list of workspace service codes your customerEligibilityPolicy checks (Keycloak claim codes, e.g. what /auth/dev's 'Workspace services' field sends) — leave empty only with the template's allow-all policy. The token is signed with the existing NEXTAUTH_SECRET. For AWS deploys add both to the task definition environment (infra/lib/stack.ts) like any other non-secret flag.

seams: src/modules/customer_preview/config/subject.ts — resolvePreviewSubject(companyId) → { companyId, accountId, name, workspaces[{id,name,services?}], services } | null; default reads the client_catalog (when CLIENT_CATALOG_BASE_URL is set), else a company_user stub with no workspaces. Override to read local tables (the header shows the client_catalog-scaffold version). accountId must equal resolveAccountIdForCompany(companyId).
securityNotes: Read-only rule: EVERY customer mutation (server action, route handler, anything that writes on a customer's behalf) calls assertNotPreview(session) — or checks isPreviewSession(session) and returns its own error — before writing. requireCustomer additionally refuses any server-action request during a preview unless the action passes { readOnly: true }; never pass readOnly on an action that writes.

Only admin access level or SuperAdmin (active, passing requireAdmin's IP / superadmin-only checks) may start or keep a preview; the cookie is bound to the admin's email and re-checked on every request.

The narrowed workspace list only narrows: it is intersected with the company's current workspaces on every request, and the start action refuses (never drops or coerces) ids that are not the company's.
During a preview the browser's useSession() is still the ADMIN's: customer layouts and nav must decide from the server session. Customer API routes (/api/account/*) do not get the overlay.

capabilities.name: S3 Storage (images & files)
capabilities.description: Upload, process and serve images and files from a per-app S3 bucket (WebP conversion, JPEG fallback, size variants, presigned URLs). Already wired into the template's admin UI (profile images, access tables), so it is standard rather than opt-in. Access is decided by a declared prefix policy in src/modules/s3_images/config/prefixes.ts: public/ is anonymous-readable and admin-write, content/ and temp/ are authenticated, mapp-team/ is admin-write. Per-app AND per-env bucket isolation is enforced by IAM, unlike the sftp capability.

envVarSources._note: S3_BUCKET_NAME is mapp-labs-{appName}-{staging|prod} and is injected into the container by CDK (infra/lib/stack.ts) — you only set it in .env for local development. S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID/S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are local-only; in ECS the task role supplies credentials. The bucket itself is created by hand with `aws s3 mb` (docs/template/DEPLOYMENT.md), not by CDK.

seams: src/modules/s3_images/config/prefixes.ts — S3_PREFIXES declares read/write access level per key prefix; add a prefix here rather than special-casing a route
securityNotes: Access control lives ONLY in config/prefixes.ts. A new route serving S3 objects must call authorizeS3Read() from server/authorize.ts — do not re-derive rules inline, which is how /api/images and /api/files came to disagree (images served content/ anonymously while files required a session for the same prefix).

S3ImageService.getPublicUrl() returns a DIRECT S3 or CloudFront URL that bypasses the app entirely, and it is stored on the S3Image record. It fails closed only because the bucket blocks public access — verify with `aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket mapp-labs-{appName}-{env}`; all four settings must be true.
Neither /api/images/[...path] nor /api/files/[...path] is in the middleware matcher; the in-route authorization is the only gate.
Never cast the `path` upload field — use parsePathName(). Casting it previously produced keys literally beginning "undefined".

capabilities.name: SFTP
capabilities.description: File exchange with ONE external SFTP endpoint via an app-owned service account, for counterparties that only speak SFTP (customer feed drops, partner exports). All access is confined to a per-app directory ({SFTP_ROOT_PATH}/{appName}), mirroring data_sync's per-app S3 prefix isolation — but enforced in code, not by IAM, so a server-side chroot of the service account is the real boundary. Host key is pinned. Not a general file store: prefer S3 / data_sync when you control both ends.

envVarSources._note: There is no shared Mapp SFTP endpoint — these are per-app, per-counterparty values. Ask the app owner or the team operating the remote host; do not invent them. SFTP_HOST_FINGERPRINT is obtained, not assigned: `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 $SFTP_HOST | ssh-keygen -lf -`. One credential must be supplied: SFTP_PASSWORD or SFTP_PRIVATE_KEY.

seams: src/modules/sftp/lib/policy.ts — sftpPolicy (allowWrites, allowedUploadExtensions, maxFileBytes); template default allows reads and writes with a data-interchange extension allowlist and a 25MB cap
securityNotes: Per-app confinement is enforced in code (src/modules/sftp/lib/paths.ts), NOT by IAM as in data_sync. Chroot the SFTP service account to the app's directory — that is the real boundary.
Every export of src/modules/sftp/lib/actions.ts is a public POST endpoint via 'use server', regardless of whether any component references it. Every one must start with an auth guard.
Do not add a customer-facing action by relaxing the admin guard: the service account's read scope is the app's, so any caller reaching an ungated action inherits all of it.

capabilities.name: User Feedback
capabilities.description: In-app feedback widget for authenticated users. Writes each entry (rating, comment, category) straight to a shared Notion 'App Feedback' database, with reporter identity, app name, responsible person (app.config.json createdBy), and company auto-filled. No Prisma model — Notion is the system of record. No LLM in the app: a centralized Notion agent handles triage/categorization/digest out of band.
